01 / THE QUESTION

Which AI careers let me combine
technical building with human connection?

My preferred direction is AI forward-deployed engineering: understanding a customer’s workflow, building a solution, and helping it work in practice. I’m comparing it with two alternatives that connect business needs to technology.

Research method: Compare three employer examples, identify requirements and eligibility limits, map them against my résumé, and propose portfolio evidence. These are November 2026 observations, not predictions of January 2029 openings. My professor’s rubric has not been provided; the structure follows the supplied peer example.

Employer example

Netic · FDE, New Grad 2026–2027
San Francisco · On-site
Advertised compensation: $138,000–$160,000.

The indexed employer description emphasizes customer workflows, AI agents, deployment, evaluation, Python and TypeScript.

Why it fits me

My customer-facing experience and programming foundation could support this combination of discovery and implementation. This is a career-fit inference, not proof of engineering readiness.

Gap & eligibility

I need stronger APIs, TypeScript, RAG evaluation, cloud deployment, and debugging evidence. The listed winter 2026–summer 2027 start window does not align with my January 2029 graduation.

Source, limitations & portfolio proof

Original Netic posting ↗ · Employer listing text available through the search index; direct page requires JavaScript. Recheck before relying on availability or terms.

Proposed proof: A service-business knowledge assistant with source references, an evaluation set, a deployment guide, and a recorded customer-workflow demo.

02
LONGER-TERM ALTERNATIVE

AI Solutions Architect

Translate business needs into a clear, testable technical design.

Compare this path ↗

Employer example

Anthropic · Applied AI Architect, Commercial
San Francisco / New York City.

Customer discovery, working prototypes, evaluations, and enterprise integration. Advertised annual range: $240,000–$315,000; the posting explains that sales-role ranges are OTE, which includes target variable pay.

Why it fits me

Presenting, teaching, and explaining choices could transfer to technical workshops. Information Systems gives me a relevant lens for connecting workflows with technology.

Gap & eligibility

The posting asks for 3+ years in technical or solutions roles and strong hands-on building. I would treat this as a future target, using internships or associate solutions roles as possible stepping stones.

Source, limitations & portfolio proof

Original Anthropic posting ↗ · Direct employer-hosted description reviewed November 17, 2026. Office attendance and travel expectations apply; verify the latest terms.

Proposed proof: A working AI demo, architecture diagram, requirements brief, cost and reliability tradeoffs, and a five-minute workshop for a nontechnical audience.

03
ALTERNATIVE ENTRY DIRECTION

AI Business Analyst / Tech & AI Consultant

Find the right problem before choosing the technology.

Compare this path ↗

Employer example

McKinsey · Business Analyst – Tech & AI
Multiple offices, including New Jersey.

Client interviews, data analysis, research, and transformation work. The accessible description does not give a numeric salary range.

Why it fits me

My operational, team-coordination, and presentation experience could help me document needs and explain recommendations. This may offer a business-centered route toward AI implementation.

Gap & eligibility

The posting requests a technical undergraduate degree and up to 3 years of experience. Whether my IS program qualifies needs confirmation. I should develop SQL, process mapping, quantitative analysis, and consulting-case skills.

Source, limitations & portfolio proof

Original McKinsey posting, job 113526 ↗ · Direct description reviewed November 17, 2026. It includes both technology and nontechnology work; an AI-only assignment is not guaranteed. Travel and schedule flexibility are listed.

Proposed proof: An AI workflow opportunity assessment with stakeholder questions, a process map, measurable success criteria, and a small dashboard built from synthetic data.

Option B: A project-first page emphasizing demos, architecture, evaluation, and decisions.

My peer-review test

  4. Once projects exist, can they find code, tests, and my contribution?
